key_insight: UniSlider makes image-editing sliders feel much more natural by aligning slider movement with perceived visual change, rather than with an arbitrary model strength parameter. This creates smoother, more predictable edits across the full range of the control.
problem_solved: Current AI image-editing sliders are usually just rescaled strength parameters, which do not correspond well to how much the image actually changes. As a result, users see uneven behavior: no visible effect for long stretches, sudden jumps, or even partial reversions as the slider moves.
method: Redefines the slider mapping so equal slider steps produce more uniform perceptual changes in the edited image.
Transforms the underlying model strength/control parameter into a perceptually calibrated interface for continuous editing.
Aims to remove dead zones and abrupt transitions by improving monotonicity and consistency of visual change.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this improves usability and trust in generative editing tools by making controls easier to interpret and tune. It can help create more professional, intuitive interfaces for creative workflows and interactive image manipulation.

paper_title: UniSlider: Perceptually Uniform Sliders for Continuous Image Editing
paper_authors: David Serrano-Lozano, Duygu Ceylan, Yannick Hold-Geoffroy, Iliyan Georgiev, Javier Vazquez-Corral
